column1: # realized_kernel_jitter_lag_length fixture data — Octave/MATLAB reference for parity testing
# Source: realized/realized_kernel_jitter_lag_length.m — Optimal endpoint jitter lag length
#   noiseEstimate: Estimated variance of microstructure noise (non-negative scalar)
#   N:             Number of price observations (positive integer)
#   jitterLags:    Optimal number of endpoint jitter lags (integer >= 1)
#   2. Compute asymptotic variance (avar) based on kernelType:
#      - kernelType=1 (flat-top n^{1/4}): avar = 16/3 * g * noise * IQ^{3/4}
#      - kernelType=2 (flat-top n^{1/6}): avar = 6 * cStar * k00 * noise^{4/3} * IQ^{2/3}
#      - kernelType=3 (non-flat-top n^{1/5}): avar = 5 * cStar * k00 * noise^{4/5} * IQ^{4/5}
#   3. Minimize MSE(m) = 8 * noise^2 * m^{-2} + avar * (N-m)^{-2*power} for m=1
#   'tukeyhanning' in Python maps to 'thinf' in MATLAB source (Tukey-Hanning kernel with
#   infinite lag order). The MATLAB function uses 'thinf'; the Python implementation accepts
#   - jitterLags is always an integer (argmin index from MSE grid search over m=1..N-1)
#   - When noise is small relative to IQ and N
